minideed.title: MiniDeed
minideed.stand: A social app where every like was worth a penny to charity. My first company, built while I was an apprentice at Goldman Sachs.
proof: raised, all of it to charity

beats.say: It started in a basement prayer room. Mehti prayed next to me every day at Goldman and one afternoon on the way out I asked how he was doing. I meant it as a greeting. He heard it as a question about his startup and told me everything.
posts: The best thing I did at Goldman Sachs was talk my way onto

beats.say: The idea was simple enough to explain in one line, which is usually a good sign. You see a cause, you feel helpless, all you can do is raise awareness. So we made the awareness itself worth something.
posts: You ever see a cause on social media and feel helpless

beats.say: I was eighteen and had no idea what I was doing, so I kept showing it to people.
posts: never I thought I’d read minideed praise in another language
Having a lot of fun presenting @MiniDeed

beats.say: People started using it to talk about what they were struggling with. I did not design that.
posts: MiniDeed is really precious tonight

beats.say: Then the number that still surprises me. Twenty five countries and £26,000, raised entirely through likes, by people who mostly had never donated to anything before.
posts: This MiniDeed journey has been amazing

beats.say: Here is what I got wrong. We removed follower counts because they felt toxic, and people churned because we had taken away the thing they came for. You cannot opt out of the attention economy by pretending it is not there.
posts: We raised £26,000 for charity through an app where every like

beats.say: It still takes donations daily, years after we stopped touching it. Sadaqah jariyah beats MRR. I kept the mug.

posts.m: In love with my new desk
posts.alt: My desk with the MiniDeed mug on it.

simply-smashed.title: Simply Smashed
simply-smashed.stand: A smashed burger joint I started with my brother in the back of a flower shop. It became London's highest rated on Google.

beats.say: We did not plan any of this. The pandemic shut my dad's restaurant, my parents were stranded in Bangladesh, and me and my brother had a kitchen and nothing to cook in it.
posts: I didn’t plan to build Simply Smashed
We sold burgers from the back of a flower shop

beats.say: A £100 grill, a borrowed projector, my mum's recipes.
posts: Three years ago, we borrowed a projector

beats.say: The part nobody claps for is the part I am proudest of. Fifty minutes down to eight.
posts: We went from 50-minute order times to 8 minutes
8am on a bank holiday Monday

beats.say: We kept making decisions that looked commercially stupid. Closing the first week of Ramadan at 30% of monthly revenue. Building a prayer space instead of more covers. Every one paid us back.
posts: Why we're closing our restaurant for the first week of Ramadan
The UK has a prayer space problem
We ban men from eating at our restaurant

beats.say: Then a landlord told us we had to sell beer. We said no and walked away from the site.
posts: The landlord had one requirement: sell beer

beats.say: We were vocal about Palestine and got review bombed for it. We doubled down.
posts: We got review bombed for supporting Palestine
"You're the Palestinian burger guy, right?"

beats.say: Two brothers recited the entire Qur'an from memory in nine hours, two seconds apart.
posts: These teenage brothers just recited the entire Quran from memory
This weekend, I’ve been building something I’ve dreamed about for years

beats.say: Somewhere in the middle of all this my face became a Ramadan meme, globally, without my permission. Fair enough.
posts: Yes. I am the face of that meme

beats.say: A customer reported a missing item, so I hired a Boris bike and cycled it to his door myself in five minutes. He took the bag without a word and shut the door. The game is the game.
posts: I once hired a Boris bike to deliver a missing chicken burger

beats.say: I left in January 2026. My brother runs it now, and runs it better.
posts: I've left Simply Smashed. After 2 years of building the highest rated

psk.title: Peruvian Street Kitchen
psk.stand: Peruvian chicken and rice, built around a green sauce I spent months failing to recreate. My brother runs it now.
proof: to sell out the first drop

beats.say: There was a lunch place near the office in my Goldman days that I could not stop thinking about, years after I stopped working there. The whole business exists because of a sauce I could not reverse engineer.
posts: There's this lunch from my Goldman days I can't get out of my head. After 16 failed

beats.say: Simply Smashed meant entering a market with a smashed burger place on every corner and trying to be better than all of them. This was the opposite problem. Nobody was asking for it, so the job was to make people want a thing they had never had.
posts: I'm building @PSK_UKI because I want to bring some new flavours
Proud to announce our newest food brand

note.txt: ai slop, i know. we just didn’t have pictures yet

beats.say: Two months between the first box and the one we launched with. That gap is the job.
posts: Left photo: Our first PSK box

posts.m: First look of Peruvian Street Kitchen
posts.alt: The first Peruvian Street Kitchen box, chicken and rice under green sauce.

note.txt: until we did. and it tasted as good as it looked

beats.say: We ran a stealth test before opening properly. Someone spent £100 trying to sabotage it, which I took as a compliment. A dad tried to buy from us five times in one week and we were shut every time.
posts: Someone spent £100 trying to sabotage my stealth launch
A dad tried to buy chicken and rice from me 5 times in one week

beats.say: Running burgers and rice boxes out of one kitchen was chaos, and I found that out the way I find most things out.
posts: Running burgers and rice boxes from the same kitchen

draper.title: Draper
draper.stand: We turn founders into industry authorities. Me, Mustafa and Aaquib.

beats.say: For the last two years of the restaurant I was quietly advising Series A founders on their content on the side. Nobody knew. I was taking calls with YC founders between burger orders.
posts: I've been lying to you. Every time you saw me at Simply Smashed

beats.say: I got more out of running the restaurant than out of anything else I have built. Then I wanted to build the thing that scaled it.
posts: I built the highest rated burger joint in London. 4.9 stars, 3000+ reviews. Those two years
I was building an AI company between burger orders

beats.say: The thesis I keep repeating, to the point that Mustafa has told me to stop. We ran a burger joint to the top of London on zero paid marketing by documenting the mess of building it. The documenting was the product.
posts: Content is product. Product is content.

beats.say: Most AI content is slop, and everyone can feel it while scrolling even if they cannot name why. The point of AI here is to sound more like yourself, not less.
posts: Let's address the elephant in the room - most AI content is garbage
I've been using AI wrong this whole time

beats.say: Mustafa brought a deep work system over from his old agency. I thought it was rigid. It doubled our focus time without adding an hour to the week and it cost nothing.
posts: We 2x'd our deep work without adding a single hour

beats.say: On the division of labour, there is not much to add.
posts: I'm the leg. Mustafa's the arm

beats.say: You can open Claude right now and start building in a field you know nothing about. Twice now, and I would do it again.
posts: I keep entering domains the slow way

clients.said: Draper is quietly becoming indispensable. That's the best compliment I can give.
Traced enterprise contracts directly to Draper, plus top talent reaching out to Sahl AI.
Something is working. You guys really tickled the algorithm there.

draper.ask: If you want this run for you, book a call. First post goes live in seven days.

bilal.title: Bilal
bilal.stand: Masjid times on my living room TV, with the athan going off at leave-time rather than prayer-time.

beats.say: It started as a question I posted rather than a product. In Muslim countries the athan comes off the minaret and you get up and go. On your phone it just becomes another notification you swipe away.
posts: if you hear the athan out loud according to Jama'ah times
when you hear the athan from minarets in Muslim countries

beats.say: A fortnight later I was testing it. That is usually the whole distance between me having a thought and me having a thing.
posts: started doing early testing of project Bilal

beats.say: It runs on a TV in my front room now, and it is up at bilalathan.co.uk if you want to point a screen at it. One household so far. Mine.
posts: im so excited to ship project bilal man

vibenasheeds.title: vibenasheeds
vibenasheeds.stand: Halal music generation. An AI that composes a track and then strips the music back out of it.
proof: between the complaint and the fix

beats.say: I have been complaining about this for eight years, which is documented and slightly embarrassing.
posts: native deen dropped so many bangers
nasheeds have regressed so much man

beats.say: Every Muslim creator hits the same wall. Use beats you are not comfortable with, or post in silence.
posts: Every Muslim creator faces the same impossible choice

beats.say: So I built the thing. It writes the music, then removes the music from itself, which is a stupid sentence and an accurate one.
posts: Side project of the week: I built an AI that composes music

lofi-muslim.title: Lofi Muslim
lofi-muslim.stand: Vocals and daf, no melodic instruments. Made as a hobby, released on YouTube, closed in January 2026. You can hear it below.

beats.say: A side-quest that got out of hand in the good way. Vocals only, no instruments, made because I wanted something I could actually put on.
The peak was a mate playing them in the background at his wedding. Nothing I have shipped since has felt quite like that.
Then I stopped. It had been a fun ride and I had run out of things to say in it.
posts: This is going to be my last beat

tracks.n: For when you need the room to settle.

simply-clo.title: SIMPLYCLO
simply-clo.stand: A clothing line. One Palestine collection, made in Bangladesh, then wound down properly.
proof: to sell out the first drop

beats.say: Eight years earlier I had worked as a graphic designer at a textile factory outside Dhaka. I went back to the same team to make a hoodie.
posts: FIRST SAMPLE CREATED WE ARE COOKING

beats.say: The Liberation Hoodie. All profits to Gaza, sold out in three hours, and the best boycott is having somewhere else to go.
posts: THE LIBERATION HOODIE 21.12.23

beats.say: Then I closed it. Bootstrapping clothing meant production delays at every single step and I would rather end something cleanly than let it rot. Killing a venture well is underrated.
posts: Fear of God's Essentials hoodie retails at £180

simply-foundation.title: Simply Foundation
simply-foundation.stand: A boarding school funded out of burger profits. Four huffadh so far.

beats.say: Our family had been quietly running a madrasah for a couple of years before we said anything publicly about it.
posts: For the last couple years our family has built our own madrasah

beats.say: Then we made it official and tied it to the business, so the burgers paid for the school.
posts: Proud to announce the public launch of our charity

beats.say: The best day of it: two brothers reciting the entire Qur'an from memory in nine hours, finishing two seconds apart.
posts: These teenage brothers just recited the entire Quran from memory

dhikry.title: dhikry
dhikry.stand: Dhikr with your closest circle. Invite only, on iOS.

beats.say: This one has no build log. I have not posted about it once, which for me is the strangest part of the whole project.
It is a small app for remembering Allah with the handful of people you actually pray for. Morning and evening, your circle, nothing else in it.
If you are in the circle you already have it. If you are not, that is rather the point.
